item.title: Samsung breaks ground on $4.5B HBM packaging plant
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: Samsung Electronics has broken ground on a 6 trillion won HBM packaging plant in Asan, South Korea, with operations planned for June 2028.
item.content:encoded:
Samsung Electronics has broken ground on a 6 trillion won ($4.48 billion) high-bandwidth memory packaging plant in Asan, South Korea, expanding a key part of Asia’s supply chain for artificial intelligence servers.

The new facility at Samsung’s Onyang campus will add advanced packaging capacity for HBM, which combines stacked memory dies with high-speed connections for AI accelerators. South Korea’s Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources announced the groundbreaking on November 12 as the first construction project under the government’s regional industrial mega-project program.

Samsung plans to follow the 6 trillion won construction investment with about 40 trillion won in advanced equipment installed in stages, taking the medium- and long-term investment associated with the Onyang HBM expansion to roughly 46 trillion won. The new line is scheduled to begin operations in June 2028, a year earlier than previously planned.

The facility will have three clean-room floors covering about 31,000 square meters. Samsung is bringing the opening forward as demand rises for server memory used in AI systems. The company said during its third-quarter earnings announcement that it had completed negotiations over HBM supply volumes for 2027 while customers continued to seek additional supply, Reuters reported.

Advanced packaging is a separate manufacturing step from producing memory wafers. It connects stacked memory with processors and other components, making packaging capacity an important constraint on finished HBM supply.

Chungcheong manufacturing expansion

The Onyang project is part of a broader investment program across South Korea’s Chungcheong region. The ministry said Samsung Electro-Mechanics is investing 8 trillion won in package-substrate production for graphics processors and central processing units, while Samsung Display is investing 67 trillion won in an 8.6-generation production line for information technology displays.

Samsung Electro-Mechanics separately disclosed in September that it would invest 4.27 trillion won in South Korea and 2.51 trillion won in Vietnam to expand flip-chip ball grid array substrates for AI servers and other high-performance computing applications. That expansion is scheduled to start mass production in September 2028.

The South Korean government said it would support the new industrial projects by coordinating permits and helping secure electricity, water and transport infrastructure. It also identified 112 materials, components and equipment suppliers with additional investment plans totaling about 23.6 trillion won around the Chungcheong projects.

Samsung has not disclosed the new Onyang plant’s planned output capacity, customer commitments or expected financial returns. The investment will be deployed over several years, with the 40 trillion won equipment component following the construction spending in phases.

Samsung Electro-Mechanics to invest $4.9B in AI-chip substrates, including $1.8B for Vietnam

item.title: EHang completes Sri Lanka’s first human-carrying eVTOL flights
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.category: Civil Aviation Authority of Sri Lanka
Sri Lanka Ministry of Ports and Civil Aviation
item.description: EHang's EH216-S completed Sri Lanka's first human-carrying eVTOL flights as regulators began practical validation for potential future operations.
item.content:encoded:
China’s EHang has completed Sri Lanka’s first human-carrying electric vertical takeoff and landing flights, moving its local program from regulatory planning into flight validation.

The EH216-S pilotless aircraft flew a coastal loop in Colombo on November 11 with Sri Lankan government and aviation officials aboard, according to EHang’s November 12 announcement. The company described the flights as the first human-carrying operation by its pilotless eVTOL in South Asia.

Sri Lanka’s ports and civil aviation minister, deputy minister and ministry secretary were among the participants. The Civil Aviation Authority of Sri Lanka also attended the event and will oversee further testing and operational validation.

The flights are part of EHang’s Global Fast Track Program, which Sri Lanka adopted in August. The framework is intended to help regulators assess aircraft performance, operating procedures, safety requirements and potential uses before deciding whether to authorize commercial services.

The aircraft has received type, production and standard airworthiness certificates in China. Those approvals establish its status in EHang’s home market but do not replace Sri Lanka’s own regulatory assessment or authorize local passenger services.

Validation before commercial approval

EHang and its local partners plan additional flight tests and data collection for regulatory review. Potential applications discussed by the company and Sri Lankan officials include aerial tourism, airport transfers, search and rescue, disaster response and service to hard-to-reach areas.

The November flights do not authorize fare-paying passenger operations. EHang did not announce a commercial launch date, approved routes, fleet size, local operator, pricing, investment amount or certification decision from Sri Lankan authorities.

TNGlobal previously reported that EHang opened a Thailand hub for its regional eVTOL rollout. At the time, the company expected Sri Lankan validation flights in November and said future operations remained subject to local laws, safety assessments and operating approvals.

The Sri Lankan program originally identified Port City Colombo as a potential sandbox area. Other possible routes and uses remain proposals rather than approved services, and the latest announcement did not confirm an operating zone beyond the demonstration route.

EHang said its EH216 series has completed nearly 100,000 flights across 24 countries. Those aggregate figures are company-supplied and include test, demonstration and other operations rather than only commercial passenger services.

The company will continue working with the Civil Aviation Authority of Sri Lanka on technical and operational assessments. Any commercial deployment would require the authority to complete its review and grant the necessary approvals.

EHang opens Thailand hub for Southeast Asia eVTOL rollout

item.title: Nvidia reaffirms 260,000-GPU supply plan for South Korea
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.category: South Korea Ministry of Science and ICT
item.description: Nvidia has reaffirmed plans to supply more than 260,000 GPUs to South Korea and continue joint AI infrastructure and research programs.
item.content:encoded:
Nvidia has reaffirmed plans to supply more than 260,000 graphics processing units to South Korea, keeping a major national artificial intelligence infrastructure program on track after the company’s leadership change.

South Korean Science and ICT Minister Bae Kyung-hoon said the ministry met Nvidia on November 13 to review the supply program and other cooperation projects. Nvidia confirmed that the commitments were company-level plans and would continue as announced.

The assurance covers both public-sector procurement and planned deployments by large Korean companies. Bae said the government has secured about 21,000 of the roughly 35,000 GPUs it intends to obtain directly from Nvidia, measured in Nvidia B200 equivalents. The remaining 14,000 are expected to arrive by early 2027.

South Korea also plans to secure the equivalent of another 15,000 GPUs through the National AI Computing Center, bringing the government’s allocation to more than 50,000 units.

The broader supply plan was first announced in October 2025. An Nvidia statement said Samsung Electronics, SK Group and Hyundai Motor Group would each build AI infrastructure using more than 50,000 GPUs, while NAVER Cloud planned to deploy more than 60,000. The government portion would support sovereign AI projects, cloud providers, research institutes, startups and universities.

A Korean government account of the original agreement said the public and private sectors would use the systems for national AI computing, foundation models, industrial applications and physical AI.

Nvidia described the planned buildout as a mix of sovereign cloud capacity and company-operated AI factories. The announced private deployments cover semiconductor manufacturing, automotive systems, robotics, telecommunications and enterprise cloud services, linking the hardware program to several of South Korea’s largest technology and industrial groups.

Bae said the two sides also intend to continue technical cooperation beyond the hardware deliveries. Planned work includes connecting Korean-designed AI accelerators with Nvidia infrastructure through NVLink, developing AI computing capacity, conducting physical AI research and training specialized workers.

The ministry will continue monitoring GPU supply and demand across the public and private sectors. It said the government-procured capacity is intended for companies, universities and research institutions, including teams working on South Korea’s sovereign foundation-model and AI-for-all initiatives.

The reaffirmation comes as South Korea expands several Nvidia-linked infrastructure programs. TNGlobal reported on November 10 that Nvidia, SK Telecom and Korean chip developer Rebellions plan to connect locally designed neural processing units with Nvidia’s rack-scale infrastructure for sovereign AI systems targeted for deployment in 2028.

Nvidia, SK Telecom and Rebellions plan Korean sovereign AI systems

item.title: AI Rudder launches CALL-E voice agent for phone calls
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: Singapore-headquartered AI Rudder launched CALL-E, which lets approved AI assistant workflows place phone calls and return transcripts and evidence.
item.content:encoded:
Singapore-headquartered conversational AI company AI Rudder has launched CALL-E, a service that allows users and developers to direct AI assistants to make phone calls after receiving approval for a specific call plan.

The company said CALL-E can be used from AI assistant and developer workflows including ChatGPT, Muse, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Claude Code, Codex and Cursor. AI Rudder’s announcement describes compatibility with these interfaces; it does not announce a partnership with their operators or native integration endorsed by them.

Before dialing, the service presents the intended call plan for user approval. After the call, it returns a summary of what was agreed, a confidence assessment, supporting lines from the conversation and a transcript. AI Rudder positions the approval and evidence features as safeguards against an agent making an unauthorized call or incorrectly reporting the result.

Developers can pass the service a call objective, telephone number and requested result format through its API. CALL-E then returns a structured result tied to the call record. Acceptance of a request means that it has entered the service’s workflow; it does not by itself confirm that the recipient answered or that the requested task succeeded.

CALL-E introduces itself as an AI voice agent by default, according to the company. AI Rudder said a pre-call check is designed to block impersonation of emergency services or law-enforcement agencies. Users can change the introduction, subject to that check.

The product handles the timing of interruptions and short acknowledgments through software surrounding its underlying voice model. AI Rudder cited results from the October 2026 TurnBench Interruption leaderboard for its Helm Swift model, but this performance claim was supplied by the company and was not independently reproduced for this report.

AI Rudder said the service uses infrastructure designed around SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO 27001 controls, as well as privacy requirements including the European Union’s General Data Protection Regulation and Southeast Asian personal data protection rules. The applicability of consent, disclosure and recording requirements varies by jurisdiction and use case.

AI Rudder is headquartered in Singapore and operates across China, Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines, alongside markets in Latin America. The company has previously deployed enterprise voice agents for financial-services workflows in Southeast Asia.

CALL-E is available through its website and API. AI Rudder said new accounts receive 100 free credits, while subsequent usage is charged according to call duration and telecommunications costs.

JCL Credit Leasing Strengthens Digital Innovation with AI Rudder’s AI Voice Agents, Advancing Malaysia’s Consumer Finance Industry

item.title: Four Southeast Asian Central Banks sign MOU to strengthen local currency transactions
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM), Bank Indonesia (BI), Bank of Thailand (BOT), and Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on cooperation under the Local Currency Transaction (LCT) Framework on Friday.
item.content:encoded:
Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM), Bank Indonesia (BI), Bank of Thailand (BOT), and Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on cooperation under the Local Currency Transaction (LCT) Framework on Friday.

The new MoU establishes a framework for cooperation among the four central banks to promote and facilitate the use of local currencies in the settlement of bilateral transactions between the participating jurisdictions, including trade, investment, and other eligible transactions, the central banks said in a statement.

It supersedes the previous bilateral MoUs on Framework for Cooperation to Promote Bilateral Transactions in Local Currencies concluded among BNM, BI, and BOT in August 2023.

By encouraging the wider use of local currencies in regional transactions, the framework aims to enhance efficiency in cross-border settlements, reduce costs associated with multiple currency conversions, and provide businesses and other market participants with greater flexibility in managing foreign exchange risks.

The participating central banks will continue to collaborate in advancing the development and implementation of the LCT Framework. The initiative is expected to gradually expand local currency transactions to support economic activities and strengthen regional financial cooperation and economic resilience.

The MoU was signed by BNM Governor Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour, BI Governor Destry Damayanti, BOT Governor Vitai Ratanakorn, and BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona, Jr.

Bank of England, MAS and Bank of Thailand complete trial of synchronized cross-currency FX settlement

item.title: UK, Singapore and Thailand central banks complete trial of synchronized cross-currency FX settlement
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: The Bank of England, Monetary Authority of Singapore, and Bank of Thailand said Friday they have completed trial of synchronized foreign exchange (FX) settlement across different currencies and systems.
item.content:encoded:
The Bank of England, Monetary Authority of Singapore, and Bank of Thailand said Friday they have completed trial of synchronized foreign exchange (FX) settlement across different currencies and systems.

The central banks said in a statement that they have published the findings from their collaboration on synchronized cross-border FX settlement under Project Meridian FX APAC.

The project marks significant progress in exploring the practical application of synchronization to FX settlement, demonstrating how it could be one approach to supporting interoperability across wholesale settlement environments built on different technologies and operating models.

Building on earlier work, Project Meridian FX APAC tested payment-versus-payment FX settlement and multilateral net FX settlement across three central banks’ test environments, spanning both Real-Time Gross Settlement and Distributed Ledger Technology based settlement systems.

The project encompassed a wider range of currencies, technologies, infrastructures and time zones. Partior, the project’s delivery partner, developed, integrated and tested the Synchronization Operator (SO) prototype for the trial.

The trial demonstrated that synchronized settlement can be achieved across central bank systems with different technologies and capabilities, while identifying the functional requirements and integration trade-offs involved. They also demonstrated how multilateral net FX settlement through synchronization can reduce settlement risk while delivering liquidity efficiencies.

The project also examined the legal, regulatory and oversight considerations for applying synchronized FX settlement in practice. The analysis was informed by perspectives from the Reserve Bank of Australia and Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, who participated as observer central banks.

The project’s findings and insights are published across three complementary reports: Executive Summary and Introduction, Technical Report, and Policy Report.

Together, they set out the experimental results, key technical findings and policy considerations.

These results provide insights to inform further exploration of synchronization as a means for enabling safer and more efficient FX settlement across diverse wholesale settlement systems.

Future work could involve extending the existing approach to additional jurisdictions and industry participants, a wider range of currencies and transaction scenarios and further consider the technical, legal, operational and governance arrangements needed in practice.

“Innovation has the greatest impact when it addresses real world challenges. Project Meridian FX APAC provides practical evidence of how synchronized settlement could help reduce risk and improve efficiency in cross-border FX transactions,

“The results provide a strong foundation for further collaboration as we explore how this approach could be developed towards real-world use,” said Tom Mutton, Executive Director of Payments, Innovation and Fintech at the Bank of England.

Kenneth Gay, Chief FinTech Officer at the Monetary Authority of Singapore, said cross-border settlement increasingly takes place across systems built on different technologies and operating models.

“Project Meridian FX APAC has shown how synchronization could help enable PvP settlement across these diverse environments, reducing settlement risk
while supporting greater interoperability,” he added.

Pucktada Treeratpituk, Director of Payment Systems and Financial Technology Policy Department at the Bank of Thailand, said project Meridian FX APAC successfully demonstrated that synchronisation can work across diverse wholesale settlement systems, making cross-border FX safer and more efficient while preserving trust in central bank money.

“The insights on technical integration, operating models and regulatory considerations established a practical foundation for modernising wholesale settlement infrastructure,” he added.

Singapore launches SPIRE Asia, targeting $500M to fund Southeast Asian farm climate resilience

item.title: Singapore sees threefold rise in reported cyber incidents since September, CSA warns
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: The average monthly number of reported cyber incidents in Singapore has tripled since September compared with the January-August period, prompting the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA) to urge organizations to strengthen their cyber defenses against increasingly opportunistic attacks.
item.content:encoded:
The average monthly number of reported cyber incidents in Singapore has tripled since September compared with the January-August period, prompting the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA) to urge organizations to strengthen their cyber defenses against increasingly opportunistic attacks.

CSA said in a statement on Friday that it has been closely monitoring these developments. It noted these incidents do not appear to be part of coordinated campaigns targeting Singapore but reflect a broader global trend of opportunistic attacks.

Some incidents have also involved compromised third-party suppliers, underscoring the importance of managing supply-chain risks, it added.

CSA, therefore, urges all organizations to take immediate steps to strengthen their cyber defenses, as cyber threat actors increasingly exploit exposed vulnerabilities and poorly secured systems.

“Cyberattacks are increasingly opportunistic. Threat actors actively scan the Internet for vulnerable systems, and organizations can become victims even if they are not specifically targeted,

“The growing use of artificial intelligence by threat actors could further accelerate the discovery and exploitation of vulnerabilities, reducing the time organizations have to secure their systems,” it said.

It also said that all organizations, regardless of size or sector, should take steps now to protect themselves.

In particular, CSA urges organizations to prioritize securing internet-facing systems, promptly patching known vulnerabilities, implementing multi-factor authentication, and monitoring for suspicious activities.

“Organizations should also ensure that their business continuity plans are ready to be activated in the event of a cyber incident,” it said.

SA has also briefed all Critical Information Infrastructure sectors and is working closely with CII Owners to strengthen their cyber defenses.

It has also engaged key Trade Associations and Chambers to help businesses understand the evolving threats and take appropriate preventive measures.

Organizations are also encouraged to tap on CSA’s CISO-as-a-Service program to engage professional consultants to develop tailored cybersecurity plans, with up to 70 percent co-funding available to eligible small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).

Singapore healthcare sector hit by cyber incidents; government steps up vigilance

item.title: NAVER signs $1.5B AI computing contract with US customer
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: NAVER has signed a 2 trillion won AI computing-services contract with an unnamed US inference company ahead of its AI Factory launch in 2027.
item.content:encoded:
South Korea’s NAVER has signed a computing-services contract worth about 2 trillion won ($1.5 billion) with an unidentified US artificial intelligence inference company, securing an initial customer for its AI Factory infrastructure business.

NAVER disclosed the contract during its third-quarter earnings call on November 12. The company said the agreement covers next-generation graphics-processing capacity and represents about 20 megawatts of service demand, according to reports by Yonhap, Newsis and other Korean business publications.

NAVER’s official third-quarter earnings presentation said customer contracts had been signed for capacity scheduled to come online in early 2027. The presentation did not identify the customer or reproduce the contract’s detailed terms.

The company expects commercial service and associated revenue to begin in the first half of 2027. It said it is also discussing additional supply agreements with more than 10 prospective customers, including AI companies outside Asia.

AI Factory moves toward commercial service

The contract builds on NAVER’s infrastructure agreements with NVIDIA and Brookfield. NAVER previously said Brookfield would invest up to $9 billion through an infrastructure vehicle that would acquire graphics processors and data-center assets for NAVER Cloud to use.

Under that structure, the Brookfield-backed vehicle would own the computing assets and charge NAVER Cloud usage fees linked to business revenue. NAVER has agreed to guarantee its subsidiary’s usage-fee obligations for up to eight years, although the company said the guarantee does not itself create an immediate cash outflow.

NAVER plans to start its AI Factory at 55 megawatts in the first half of 2027 and expand to 200 megawatts by 2028. The company said it has secured data-center capacity beyond that 2028 target, although much of the capacity is not yet covered by disclosed customer contracts.

TNGlobal reported in July that NAVER, Brookfield and NVIDIA planned a 200-megawatt Korean AI Factory using NVIDIA computing platforms, with NAVER’s GAK Sejong data center as the main hub.

The new customer remains unnamed, and NAVER did not disclose the contract period, pricing structure, service-level obligations, cancellation terms or expected margin. It also did not say which graphics processors will be allocated to the customer beyond referring to next-generation capacity.

NAVER reported third-quarter enterprise revenue of 193.3 billion won, up 33 percent from a year earlier, while infrastructure expenses rose 29.1 percent. The company attributed part of the higher spending to computing assets and data-center rents.

NAVER Partners with Brookfield and NVIDIA to Expand Korea’s National AI Factory Infrastructure Buildout

item.title: Adaspace raises $96M in Hong Kong IPO
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: Chinese AI satellite developer Adaspace raised about $95.6 million in a Hong Kong IPO and began trading under stock code 6935.
item.content:encoded:
Chinese AI satellite developer Adaspace Technology began trading in Hong Kong on Friday after raising HK$750.01 million ($95.6 million), adding a commercial-space company to the city’s technology listings.

The Chengdu-based company sold 30.12 million H shares at HK$24.90 each, the bottom of its marketed range of HK$24.90 to HK$33.20, according to its final offer and allotment announcement filed with Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing.

The offer generated gross proceeds of HK$750.01 million and estimated net proceeds of HK$651.76 million after listing expenses. The Hong Kong public offering was 3.43 times subscribed, while the international offering was 1.79 times subscribed.

Adaspace opened at HK$24.44, 1.8 percent below its offer price. Reuters reported that the shares were trading at HK$24.60 at the time of its report, down 1.2 percent from the offer price.

Adaspace develops and produces satellites and provides satellite-based services and solutions. Its listing prospectus said revenue rose from RMB507.5 million in 2023 to RMB702.7 million in 2025. Revenue for the first six months of 2026 was RMB226.1 million, compared with RMB241.3 million a year earlier, with the company attributing the decline to the scheduling of satellite launches and deliveries in the fourth quarter.

The company remained loss-making. It reported net losses of RMB139.3 million in 2023, RMB177.2 million in 2024 and RMB255.9 million in 2025. Its net loss for the first half of 2026 was RMB150.8 million, while research and development expenses represented 48 percent of revenue during the period.

Adaspace said it intends to use the proceeds to support an AI computing satellite constellation under its Star-Compute Project, space-computing research and development, and construction of a research center in Shenzhen. The proceeds may also fund selected investments or acquisitions, debt repayment and working capital.

The prospectus said 35 satellites developed by the company had been launched, including 29 described as AI satellites. Those operating and technology milestones are company disclosures and were not independently assessed in the offer results.

The listing follows Hong Kong’s efforts to attract more specialist technology issuers. Adaspace trades on the exchange’s Main Board under stock code 6935.

item.title: Geotab launches asset tracker in the Philippines
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: Geotab has launched its GO Anywhere Plus tracker in the Philippines for businesses managing vehicles, equipment and other distributed assets.
item.content:encoded:
Connected-operations company Geotab has launched its GO Anywhere Plus asset-tracking device in the Philippines, targeting businesses that manage equipment, trailers, containers and other assets across multiple locations.

The launch adds a Philippines-specific connected-asset product to Geotab’s Southeast Asian portfolio. The device is intended for powered and non-powered assets and integrates with the company’s MyGeotab platform, allowing organizations to view vehicles and other equipment through one system.

According to Geotab’s announcement, the tracker provides location and usage information that can support maintenance planning, deployment decisions and asset recovery. The company said the product is aimed at industries with equipment spread across construction sites, logistics networks and field operations.

The release cited Philippine Statistics Authority data showing that 10.57 million metric tons of commodities moved through domestic trade in the second quarter of 2026, with road transport accounting for 64.3 percent of the total. It also cited the value of Philippine construction projects in 2025 as P601.4 billion.

Those figures describe the scale of logistics and construction activity rather than measured demand for Geotab’s product. The company did not disclose pricing, customer commitments, sales targets or expected deployment volumes for GO Anywhere Plus in the Philippines.

The tracker extends telematics beyond fleet vehicles to equipment that may not have a vehicle diagnostic connection or continuous power supply. Geotab said customers can use the resulting data to identify underused assets, locate missing equipment and plan maintenance based on usage.

The launch follows other additions to Geotab’s regional product portfolio. The company previously introduced a fuel-monitoring harness for Southeast Asian markets, including the Philippines, and has rolled out AI-enabled video telematics products in Singapore and Thailand.

Geotab describes itself as a provider of connected transportation, video telematics and asset-tracking systems. Its platform combines data from vehicles, equipment and other operational assets for fleet management and business analysis.

The company did not identify a first customer or implementation partner for the Philippine launch. Businesses can access the product through Geotab’s local sales and partner channels, according to the announcement.

Revolutionising Fuel Management: Geotab Launches Innovative Fuel Harness for Southeast Asian Markets
